summary: Created the opsbot account on node1 and node2 (CentOS Stream 10), generated an ed25519 keypair for opsbot on node1, installed the public key into opsbot's authorized_keys on node2, and enforced key-only SSH authentication for opsbot on both nodes via a `Match User opsbot` block in sshd_config.d (PasswordAuthentication no, AuthenticationMethods publickey) plus a locked password hash. Verified opsbot@node1 can SSH into opsbot@node2 using the key, and that password auth is rejected for opsbot on both nodes. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on node1 then node2, confirming changed boot_id on each and that sshd, the sshd_config Match block, the authorized_keys file, the locked shadow entry, and cross-node key-based SSH access all survived and were re-verified after each restart.
actions_performed: Checked baseline: opsbot did not exist on either node; no pre-existing PasswordAuthentication/PubkeyAuthentication overrides
Created opsbot user + ~/.ssh dir (mode 700) on node1 and node2
Generated ed25519 keypair for opsbot on node1 (ssh-keygen, no passphrase, as opsbot)
Installed opsbot@node1's public key into /home/opsbot/.ssh/authorized_keys on node2 (mode 600, owned by opsbot)
Added /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/90-opsbot.conf on node1 and node2 with Match User opsbot block requiring publickey-only auth; validated with sshd -t
Locked opsbot's password (passwd -l) on both nodes as defense in depth
Reloaded sshd on both nodes and confirmed active
Verified opsbot@node1 -> opsbot@node2 SSH via key succeeds
Verified password-based SSH is rejected for opsbot on both nodes (falls to publickey-only, no password prompt)
Captured pre-restart boot_id, sshd status, and opsbot config on node1 and node2

Restarted node1 via backgrounded `shutdown -r now` so the exec ack returned before disconnect, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, re-verified sshd config, locked password, and opsbot identity
Restarted node2 the same way, polled until reachable, confirmed new boot_id, re-verified sshd config, authorized_keys, and locked password
Re-ran cross-node SSH key auth test (node1 opsbot -> node2 opsbot) after both restarts to confirm functional recovery

evidence.requirement: opsbot account created on node1 and node2
evidence.summary: useradd succeeded and id opsbot confirms uid 1000 opsbot exists on both nodes

evidence.requirement: SSH keypair generated for opsbot and public key installed on node2
evidence.summary: ed25519 key generated on node1 as opsbot; public key written to node2's /home/opsbot/.ssh/authorized_keys with correct ownership/perms

evidence.requirement: opsbot can run commands as opsbot on node2 via SSH key
evidence.summary: sudo -u opsbot ssh from node1 to node2's IP with BatchMode=yes succeeded, returning hostname=node2, whoami=opsbot

evidence.requirement: Key-based auth required (password auth disabled) for opsbot on both systems
evidence.summary: Match User opsbot block (PasswordAuthentication no, AuthenticationMethods publickey) added and validated on both nodes, sshd reloaded, and direct password-auth SSH attempts against opsbot@localhost on both nodes returned 'Permission denied (publickey)' with no password prompt
Captured boot_id=bccb87ac..., sshd active, opsbot present, pre-restart state

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Backgrounded shutdown -r now returned before disconnect; node1 became unreachable then reachable again; new boot_id=4f807c80... differs from baseline, proving an actual reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of opsbot config
evidence.summary: sshd active and config valid, Match User opsbot block intact, opsbot shadow entry still locked (!) after reboot
Captured boot_id=45c22b1f..., sshd active, authorized_keys present, pre-restart state

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Backgrounded shutdown -r now returned before disconnect; node2 became unreachable then reachable again; new boot_id=96cd071c... differs from baseline, proving an actual reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 post-restart recovery of opsbot config and cluster access
evidence.summary: sshd active/valid, Match block and authorized_keys intact, opsbot shadow entry still locked after reboot; end-to-end SSH from node1 opsbot to node2 opsbot succeeded post-restart
